findings.title: Missing double-check after acquiring write lock (classic double-checked locking omission)
findings.body:
After releasing the RLock and before acquiring the write Lock, another goroutine may have already computed and stored the result in `entryPointAssetsCache`. When the current goroutine finally acquires the write lock, it proceeds to re-read the manifest file (or make an HTTP request) redundantly. In production (non-dev) mode with concurrent requests at startup, this means multiple goroutines will serialize on the write lock and each perform the same expensive I/O. The standard fix is to re-check the cache immediately after acquiring the write lock:

```go
entryPointAssetsCacheMu.Lock()
defer entryPointAssetsCacheMu.Unlock()

if cfg.Env != setting.Dev && entryPointAssetsCache != nil {
    return entryPointAssetsCache, nil
}
```

This is the well-known double-checked locking pattern; without the second check the cache provides no benefit under concurrent access until the first writer finishes.
